walkthrough:
Read the Graph Shape Correctly**
Positive values on the y-axis mean the potato has gained mass and negative values mean it has lost mass. The line starts high on the left at about +12% and falls steadily as sucrose concentration increases, crossing zero at about $0.2 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$.

Split the Description at the Zero Point**
Below $0.2 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ the values are above zero, so mass increases. At $0.2 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ the line is at 0%, so no net change. Above $0.2 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ the values are below zero, so mass decreases, and the line goes more negative as concentration rises, showing a larger percentage loss.

Add Evidence With Numbers**
Always support a graph description with figures. Quote two points like with like, for example about +2% at $0.2 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ falling to about -24% at $0.6 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$, or about +12% at $0.0 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ falling to about -47% at $1.0 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$. Include $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ for concentration and % for change at least once.

Final answer: From $0$ to $0.2 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ mean percentage change is positive so mass increases; at $0.2 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ there is no change in mass; from $0.2$ to $1.0 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ mean percentage change is negative so mass decreases, with greater decrease at higher concentration. E.g. at $0.0 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ about +12% and at $1.0 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ about -47%.

hints: Check Fig. 3.2 at $0.6 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$. Is the percentage change positive or negative, and what substance moving in or out of cells would cause that mass change?
Recall the name of the process for net movement of water across the cell surface membrane, which acts as a partially permeable membrane.
Think about why water moves that way in terms of water potential inside the potato cells compared to the concentrated sucrose solution outside.
walkthrough:
Link Mass Loss to Water Loss**
At $0.6 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ the graph shows about -24% change, so the cylinder has lost mass. Plant cells gain or lose mass almost entirely by gaining or losing water, so here water must have moved out of the cells into the surrounding solution.

Name the Process and the Driving Force**
Water moves across the partially permeable cell surface membrane by osmosis. It moves down a water potential gradient, from a region of higher water potential to a region of lower water potential. The $0.6 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ sucrose solution has many solute molecules, so it has a more negative water potential than the cell sap inside the potato cells.

Connect to the Cell Effect**
As water leaves, the vacuole and cytoplasm shrink, the cell loses turgidity and the protoplast may pull away from the wall, which is plasmolysis. The whole tissue therefore weighs less after blotting dry.

Final answer: Mass decreases because water leaves the potato cells by osmosis down a water potential gradient, from higher water potential in cells to lower (more negative) water potential in $0.6 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ sucrose solution, causing loss of turgidity / plasmolysis.
